records.issue_text: In CalendarService.ts deleteEvent, the same fallback lookup logic error compares externalId against a falsy externalCalendarId, never resolving a calendar id and breaking event deletion
records.rationale: The diff changes deleteEvent (and updateEvent) fallback in googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` guarded by `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : ...`. The fallback branch executes only when externalCalendarId is falsy, so the find can never match, always yielding undefined — meaning the destination calendar is never resolved and event deletion falls back to no calendar id (unlike the old `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`). Verifiable real defect introduced by this diff.

records.issue_text: In handleNewBooking.ts, evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars) silently no-ops when evt.destinationCalendar is null, dropping team members' destination calendars for collective events where the organizer has no personal destination calendar
records.rationale: The diff sets destinationCalendar to `null` when neither eventType.destinationCalendar nor organizerUser.destinationCalendar exists, then relies on `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` to add collective team members' calendars. Optional chaining means that push silently no-ops for null, dropping teamDestinationCalendars that were collected regardless of organizer calendar presence. This is a real, verifiable mechanism in the diff: team members' destination calendars would not be applied for collective bookings whose organizer lacks a destination calendar.
